  "text": "On Sunday, Mara came home from the library at half past three. She had stayed to mend the spine of an atlas that no one had borrowed in years. Its maps showed countries with names the children no longer recognized. She left it under a stack of dictionaries while the glue dried.

At home, she put the kettle on and carried the suitcase into the hall. One wheel had seized during the walk from the station, leaving a dark line across the floorboards. She rubbed the line with her thumb. It faded a little. She set the suitcase beside the umbrella stand and went back to the kitchen.

The telephone rang at ten minutes past four.

He said he was sorry to have kept her waiting. His neighbor had needed help carrying her shopping upstairs. Mara thought of the narrow staircase in his building and the knee he had injured years ago. She asked whether the neighbor had bought anything good. Mostly tins, he said.

They talked about the book he had sent in the parcel. He remembered borrowing it, though neither of them could remember why it had stayed with him. The due-date stamp was twenty-three years old. Mara told him she had slipped it through the library’s returns slot that morning. He laughed and asked whether there would be a fine.

Not for that book, she said.

For a moment she could hear traffic at his end of the line. Then he asked if she would meet him for tea. Mara said there was a café across from the library, and Thursday was her early day.

After they hung up, she made tea with the water in the kettle. It was still warm enough."
